Interactive
Click any node to simulate a failure. If the Primary goes down, an election starts automatically. Click a failed node to bring it back online.
⏳ Election in progress 10s
The MongoDB driver may retry eligible operations automatically. Retries depend on driver options and timeouts. Once a primary is elected, operations can resume; durability depends on the write concern used.
📖 No majority — writes blocked
The replica set has lost its voting majority. Surviving secondaries may still serve reads if the read preference allows secondaries and the read concern can be satisfied. Data may be stale. Reads requiring a primary are blocked. Writes resume after a primary and a majority are available.
🔴 Complete outage — all nodes are DOWN
Every node in the replica set is unreachable. No reads or writes can be served. This is a full database outage. Restore a majority and elect a primary to resume writes; reads from a recovered secondary depend on the read settings.

RS Configuration
Write & Read Concerns
Write Concern controls durability — how many replica set nodes must confirm a write before the driver returns success. Read Concern controls data freshness — whether you see only majority-committed data or also in-flight writes. Read Preference controls which node serves the read. Adjust any setting to see how MongoDB's CAP position shifts.

⚠ 2-Region topology — quorum limitation
With 2+1 members per shard, losing the region with two members leaves only 1 of 3 votes. That shard cannot elect a primary or accept writes. With one member in each of three regions, a single-region failure leaves a majority.
Each row is one shard’s replica set; each column is a region. Dashed arrows show oplog replication from the current primary. Fail a region or click a node, then restore it to follow the recovery.
